note: Route-graph ratchet baseline (no-new-rot ratchet). Each entry is the CURRENT reachable-first-party-module-count ceiling for a LOCKED FIXED_ROUTES route (the primary dev-perf 'first-party graph pressure' metric from scripts/route-graph.mjs). The gate fails when a tracked route's count grows BEYOND its ceiling and when the committed baseline raises any ceiling vs the base branch WITHOUT a matching absorb record. Counts are captured WITH the companion extension repos cloned pinned (exactly as CI does via clone-extensions) so they reproduce in CI. Regenerate with `node scripts/audit/route-graph-ratchet.mjs --write-baseline` after cloning the extensions — a ceiling should only ever be LOWERED as barrel imports are narrowed, and is never raised SILENTLY. A sanctioned raise must be ANNOTATED: a sibling `absorbs` record `route -> { from, to, reason, pr }` whose from/to exactly match the raise vs the base branch (from = the base ceiling, to = the new committed ceiling, reason = why the growth is accepted, pr = the PR carrying the absorbed change). The gate validates records strictly (malformed/stale/orphan records fail closed; a carried-forward record may not be deleted while its raised ceiling is kept) and prints a LOUD NOTICE line for every absorbed raise. The tracked route set is route-graph.mjs FIXED_ROUTES; change it there, then regenerate.

/sign-in.reason: cinatra#2569 (epic #2564 S5) the conversational schedule PROPOSAL producer, plus the two extraction leaves the ratcheted bottleneck files forced. `schedule_proposal_render` is a first-party MCP primitive registered on the cinatra self-MCP server, which the app's auth plugins mount, so its closure lands on every locked route: the producer module, the proposal TOKEN it mints (a signed, authenticated-encrypted, expiring ref — the whole proposal, because §VI's "nothing exists until the reader confirms" leaves no row to address), the PROPOSE leaf it calls, the recurrence vocabulary the scheduling form and the server now share, and the proposal card's typed view. The remaining two are `trigger-schedule-proposal-schema.ts` (the new tables' bootstrap DDL, born in a leaf because the schema-migration gate reads deployed DDL out of drizzle-store.ts alone) and `run-co-owners-store.ts` (a verbatim vertical slice lifted out of store.ts, which sits exactly at its file-size ceiling). ALREADY NARROWED and measured at each step (+7 → +5 → +7 after the migration-gate correction restored the deployed DDL): the CONFIRM transaction, the schedule-install outbox store and the drain do NOT appear here, because propose was split into its own leaf and the Confirm/Adjust server actions were moved out of run-actions.ts into their own "use server" module beside the feature — run-actions.ts is itself reachable from the self-MCP surface, so appending to it would have put the whole confirm lane on all five routes for code only the rendered card calls. The lifecycle dispatcher's proposal arm is likewise left inert (the resolve route is its live resolver and needs the typed body too), keeping the card resolver off these graphs for a path production never takes. The remainder cannot be narrowed without giving up the slice's premises: a producer that cannot mint a token cannot propose, a recurrence vocabulary that is not SHARED with the scheduling form is a second cron translation free to disagree with the one the reader confirmed, and the two extraction leaves exist because two OTHER ratchets require them. Dynamic import buys nothing — the analyzer follows `import()` too. Counts measured with the same resolution set on both sides of the base ref (fa406a0a0): a uniform +7 on all five locked routes.
